description: Background:Vitiligo is a chronic disease that is often challenging to treat. Melanocyte destruction in vitiligo is mediated by immune pathways involving IFN-γ and CD8+ T cells. Tofacitinib, a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/3 inhibitor, can be a promising treatment for vitiligo due to its potential to inhibit IFN-γ signaling.

title: Intermediate-Controlled Synthesis of Quasi-2D (PEA)2MA4Pb5I16 in the 20–30% Relative Humidity Glovebox Environment for Fabricating Perovskite Solar Cells with 1 Month Durability in the Air
creator: Yen-Shuo Chen, Min-Han Hsieh, Ching-Chang Lin, Yi-Cheng Huang, Shang-Yu Tsai, Fu-Hsiang Ko
description: Herein, quasi-two-dimensional (Q-2D) (PEA)2MA4Pb5I16 (prepared by a two-step process) and hole transport layer of a solar cell were fabricated in a high relative humidity (25 ± 5%) environment. The PSC behavior of most Q-2D perovskites is worse than that of three-dimensional perovskites owing to the horizontal alignment of the innate characteristic organic plates on the substrate.

title: Development of a simplified NOVA-based scoring tool for assessing ultra-processed food consumption among Korean young adults: a cross-sectional study
creator: Jinhyun Kim, Eunjin Jang, Sarang Jeong, Sukyoung Jung, Jee Young Kim, Jung Eun Lee, Dahye Han, Eunseo Lee, Junhyeok Jang, Sohyun Park
description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to develop a NOVA-based scoring approach for evaluating ultra-processed food (UPF) intake among Korean adults and to examine its performance. Previous studies have reported that young adults have the highest levels of UPF consumption. Accordingly, this study focused on adults aged 19–40 years and developed scoring components reflecting dietary patterns specific to Korean eating habits.

title: Life-course personalized nutrition strategy for adolescents and young adults in Korea based on a behavioral science approach and community-based model: a narrative review
creator: Jung-Hyun Kim
description: ObjectivesThis review examines the nutritional challenges among Korean adolescents and young adults from life-course and behavioral science perspectives and proposes an integrated, community-based nutrition strategy for this critical transitional period. MethodsA narrative review was conducted following the Scale for the Quality Assessment of Narrative Review Articles guidelines.

title: Exploring Molecular Descriptors and Acquisition Functions in Bayesian Optimization for Designing Molecules with Low Hole Reorganization Energy
creator: Rinta Kawagoe, Tatsuhito Ando, Nobuyuki N Matsuzawa, Hiroyuki Maeshima, Hiromasa Kaneko
description: Organic semiconductors have been widely studied owing to their potential applications in various devices, such as field-effect transistors, light-emitting diodes, solar cells, and image sensors. However, they have a limitation of significantly lower carrier mobility compared to silicon, which is a widely used inorganic semiconductor. Therefore, to address such limitations, these molecules should be further explored.

title: Cell-specific delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 with pseudotyped lentiviral particles: Just change the envelope
creator: Ángela Covo-Vergara, Laura Salaberry, Noelia Silva-Pilipich, Sandra Hervas-Stubbs, Cristian Smerdou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). several genes in specific cell types by pseudotyping LVNPs with envelope proteins from three different viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus, and measles virus. The importance of this study lies in its demonstration that LVNPs can be readily tuned to target different cell types, which could potentially enable gene editing in vivo, although the experiments shown in this work were only performed in cell culture. Genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9 has been shown to be an extremely useful research tool with great therapeutic potential.

title: Holding the treatment frame: borderline features, personality functioning, and psychotherapy dropout in a youth mental health service
creator: Francesca De Salve, Chiara Rossi, Osmano Oasi, Lara Malvini, Maria Meliante, Mauro Percudani, Irene Messina
description: Baseline personality pathology may shape both everyday functioning and engagement in psychotherapy. This study tested whether maladaptive personality trait domains and borderline symptom severity were associated with psychosocial functioning at intake and whether these variables were related to subsequent psychotherapy dropout within the same clinical pathway. Participants were 124 young adults (M age = 20.81, SD=2.30; 51.6% male and 48.

title: Mechanisms governing bystander activation of T cells
creator: Mohammed Yosri, Mohamed Dokhan, Elizabeth Aboagye, Mouhamad Al Moussawy, Hossam A. Abdelsamed
description: The immune system is endowed with the capacity to distinguish between self and non-self, so-called immune tolerance or “consciousness of the immune system.” This type of awareness is designed to achieve host protection by eliminating cells expressing a wide range of non-self antigens including microbial-derived peptides.

title: Hounsfield unit and gray-white matter ratio estimates in pediatric normal controls used in studies evaluating head computed tomography
creator: Kie Honjo, Geraldine Goco, Eva Ta, Suzanne Laughlin, Anne-Marie Guerguerian
description: Head computed tomography (CT) plays a key diagnostic role in assessing anatomically visible cerebral injury, monitoring the development of edema and ischemia, and, in some diseases, assisting in the prediction of outcome. More specifically, after a cardiac arrest, head CT imaging will reveal the impact of global hypoxic-ischemic injury.

title: Spectroscopy-multimodal data fusion empowers smart food quality analysis: Challenges and prospects
creator: Zhanming Li, Wenxuan Deng, Jing Zhao, Yan Kong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Food quality assessment faces challenges in detecting complex samples, with single spectroscopic techniques limited in precision and applicability. Multimodal data fusion, by combining different spectroscopic techniques with non-spectroscopic data, significantly enhances the accuracy and comprehensiveness of detection. Low-, mid-, and high-level data fusion strategies offer substantial advantages in information integration and model optimization, addressing the shortcomings of single spectroscopic methods in complex food sample analysis. Multimodal data fusion has shown great potential in food adulteration detection, geographical traceability, and quality assessment.

title: Engineering β-cyclodextrin gels with nanoparticles: tunable assembly and multifunctional applications
creator: Sagar Kumar Pathak, Aiswarya Sukumaran, Ioanna Chazapi, Claire Hotton, Erwan Paineau, Ravi Kumar Pujala
description: Hierarchical gels were developed through the controlled interaction of β-cyclodextrin in good–poor solvent systems, incorporating small amounts of various nanoparticles and nanoclays. These new hierarchical microstructures form through the side-by-side aggregation of β-cyclodextrin lamellar plates. They are stabilized by non-covalent interactions and facilitated by negatively charged nanoparticles or nanoclays.

title: Risk factors of allergic rhinitis and its prevention strategies
creator: Ruzhi Chen, Wei An, Xueting Liu, Jie Yan, Yuyi Huang, Junyan Zhang
description: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a global disease with high prevalence. It reduces the patient's quality of life seriously. The health care and management of AR was also a heavy social burden. Specific immunotherapy (SIT) is the only curative treatment for AR that may alter the natural course of this disease.

title: FOXO1-mediated cell cycle arrest enhances osteogenic differentiation of spheroid-cultured human periodontal ligament–derived multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells
creator: Sho Hironaka, Satoru Onizuka, Kotaro Sano, Yuichiro Oka, Takenori Suga, Shoichiro Kokabu, Wataru Ariyoshi, Kohji Nakazawa, Shinichi Mochizuki, Michihiko Usui
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionPeriodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by progressive alveolar bone loss. Although spheroid culture enhances the osteogenic and regenerative potential of human periodontal ligament–derived multipotent mesenchymal stromal cells (hPDLMSCs), the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the transcriptional features of spheroid-cultured hPDLMSCs, with a particular focus on cell cycle regulation and Forkhead Box O (FOXO) transcription factors.MethodsMonolayer- and spheroid-cultured hPDLMSCs were subjected to transcriptome analysis using RNA sequencing.

title: Associations of lipoprotein(a) concentrations with cardiovascular disease in men and women with primary hypercholesterolemia
creator: Jakub Kurdziel, Andrzej Fedak, Agnieszka Micek, Przemysław Miarka, Maciej T. Małecki, Małgorzata Waluś-Miarka
description: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a useful marker for cardiovascular risk stratification. Previous studies have shown higher Lp(a) levels in women than in men and sex differences in its association with atherosclerosis. The aim of this study was to assess associations between Lp(a) levels and cardiovascular disease (CVD) in men and women with suspected familial hypercholesterolemia (FH).

title: Knowledge and perceptions of blood donors of the Western Cape Blood Services, South Africa, toward vaginal sample donation for biobanking
creator: Shantelle Claassen-Weitz, Brian Kullin, Elloise du Toit, Sugnet Gardner-Lubbe, Jo-Ann S. Passmore, Heather Jaspan, Anna-Ursula Happel, Greg Bellairs, Caroline Hilton, Anika Chicken, Kirsten Welp, Hannah Livingstone, Adrian Brink
description: IntroductionDepletion of Lactobacillus species and an overgrowth of anaerobes in the vaginal tract bacterial vaginosis (BV)], is associated with non-optimal reproductive health outcomes, and increased susceptibility to sexually transmitted infections (STIs). BV is currently treated with antibiotics, although these provide suboptimal cure levels and high recurrence rates.

title: Hypothalamic-superior frontal gyrus functional connectivity alterations and luteinizing hormone correlations in girls with central precocious puberty
creator: Hongqiang Cai, Lianzi Su, Xiyan Chen, Moran Yang, Jiajia Xu, Yanqi Shan, Ru Zhao, Longsheng Wang, Yue Yu, Liwei Zou
description: Purpose In this study, the neural communication patterns between hypothalamic structures and cortical areas in girls diagnosed with central precocious puberty (CPP) were explored. Endocrine profiles were incorporated to clarify the pathophysiological interactions between cerebral networks and hormonal regulation. The hypothalamus was designated as the key focus area for connectivity analysis.

title: MC4R-related monogenic obesity in children: insights from 2 cases
creator: Dhivya Shanmugam, Subbiah Sridhar, Nandini Kuppusamy, Kathirvel Manjini, Palaniappan Sreenivasan, Muthu Aravind Kumar
description: Childhood and adolescent obesity are growing global health concerns, with genetic factors playing an important role. Despite the increasing prevalence of obesity in India, monogenic obesity remains underdiagnosed. We report 2 cases of early-onset morbid obesity due to melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) gene mutation. Case 1 was a 5-year-old boy who presented with severe hyperphagia and rapid weight gain since infancy.

title: Reply Letter: A Commentary on “Disuse Bone Loss in Fusion Constructs After Multilevel Lumbar Fusion: A Computed Tomography Hounsfield Unit Analysis”
creator: Hyun-Jun Jang, Dongkyu Kim, Bong-Ju Moon, Kyung-Hyun Kim, Jeong-Yoon Park, Sung-Uk Kuh, Keun-Su Kim, Dong-Kyu Chin
description: lignment, and the need for longitudinal data are not only valid but also demonstrate the evolving understanding of mechanobiological bone remodeling in spinal surgery [2]. As the letter correctly pointed out, our study employed Hounsfield units (HU) to tackle the important issue of level-specific bone remodeling in multilevel lumbar fusion.

title: Antioxidant potential, antimicrobial activity, polyphenol profile analysis, and cytotoxicity against breast cancer cell lines of hydro-ethanolic extracts of leaves of (Ficus carica L.) from Eastern Morocco
creator: Aziz Tikent, Salah Laaraj, Toufik Bouddine, Mohamed Chebaibi, Mohamed Bouhrim, Kaoutar Elfazazi, Ali S. Alqahtani, Omar M. Noman, Lhoussain Hajji, Larbi Rhazi, Ahmed Elamrani, Mohamed Addi
description: IntroductionMany beneficial compounds found in fig leaves can be used in tea and medicine. These compounds aid with digestion, reduce inflammation, and treat diabetes and bronchitis. Chetoui, Malha, Ghoudane, and Onk Hmam fig leaf hydro-ethanol extracts from Eastern Morocco were analyzed for metabolites and biological activities.

title: The Prioritized Correction at Osteotomy Site: A Novel Technique for Preventing Sagittal Translation During 3-Column Osteotomies in Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery
creator: Chen Ling, Jie Li, Zongshan Hu, Yanjie Xu, Abdukahar Kiram, Ziyang Tang, Hui Xu, Xiaodong Qin, Benlong Shi, Zezhang Zhu, Yong Qiu, Zhen Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo compare perioperative and complication outcomes, focusing on the prevention of sagittal translation (ST), between a novel “prioritized correction with multiple-rod construct” (PC-MRC) technique and traditional multiple-rod constructs (M-RC) in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients undergoing 3-column osteotomies (3-COs). MethodsIn this retrospective study, 101 ASD patients with a minimum 2-year follow-up after 3-COs were divided into 2 groups: PC-MRC (n=65) and M-RC (n=36). The PC-MRC technique involved initial osteotomy closure with short rods followed by global alignment correction with long rods.

title: Real-Time Location System Assessment of Early Postoperative Recovery After Lumbar Decompression According to Surgical Approach
creator: Sub-Ri Park, Jaenam Lee, Sujin Kwon, Namhoo Kim, Dong Won Kim, Dukyong Yoon, Kyoung Min Kim, Byung Ho Lee
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate early postoperative mobility after lumbar decompression using real-time location system (RTLS)-derived objective metrics and to explore differences in mobility patterns between biportal endoscopic decompression and open decompression. MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 323 patients who underwent lumbar decompression for degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis between March 2020 and May 2024.

title: Occipital Bone Erosion Following C1–2 Posterior Fixation: A Comparative Per-Screw Analysis of Tan versus Harms-Goel Techniques
creator: Shigeo Ueda, Nobuaki Naito, Hokuto Yamashita, Jiro Ohara, Atsuhiko Toyoshima, Miyuki Fukuda, Nobuhiro Sasaki, Masayuki Kuroda, Minoru Hoshimaru
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the relationship between C1 screw trajectory and occipital bone erosion in C1–2 posterior fixation. MethodsThis retrospective cohort study analyzed 27 patients (54 screws) who underwent C1–2 posterior fixation between March 2018 and March 2023 at a single institution by multiple surgeons. Screws were classified by trajectory: Tan technique (n=39) or Harms-Goel (HG) technique (n=15).

title: A Commentary on “A Comprehensive Review of Spinal Arthroplasty”
creator: Sonja Häckel, Fabienne Pohle
description: valuable. By discussing cervical and lumbar disc replacement as well as lumbar facet arthroplasty together, Liu et al. [1] demonstrate that preserving motion is no longer a single concept but rather a range of reconstructive strategies with very different levels of evidence, technical maturity, and clinical readiness.

title: Effect of synbiotic supplementation on obesity and gut microbiota in obese adults: a double-blind randomized controlled trial
creator: Xiaokang Niu, Qi Zhang, Julong Liu, Yuyang Zhao, Nan Shang, Shusen Li, Yinghua Liu, Wei Xiong, Erna Sun, Yong Zhang, Hongfeng Zhao, Yixuan Li, Pengjie Wang, Bing Fang, Liang Zhao, Juan Chen, Fuqing Wang, Guofang Pang, Chenyuan Wang, Jingjing He, Ran Wang
description: BackgroundSynbiotics, combining specific probiotics and selected prebiotics, may benefit health issues like obesity, but evidence remains inconsistent.ObjectiveThis study aimed to verify the effect of a pre-screened synbiotics combination [containing Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis MN-Gup (MN-Gup), galacto-oligosaccharides (GOS) and xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS)] on obesity in the population.

title: From the Editor-in-Chief: Featured Articles in the April 2026 Issue
creator: Inbo Han
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). smartphones with conventional clinical measurement tools to evaluate the recovery trajectory of patients who underwent lumbar spine surgery for sciatica. An analysis of data over 6 months postoperatively revealed significant differences in long-term recovery tracking. While conventional objective performance measures, such as the 6-minute walk test, and patient-reported outcomes showed an initial pattern of improvement before reaching a plateau after 6 weeks, smartphone-derived activity data showed a continuous and linear increase in physical activity.

title: Stimuli-responsive 4D-bioprinted constructs for musculoskeletal tissue regeneration: Shape-morphing mechanisms, cell-laden bioink engineering, and preclinical outcomes
creator: Suleiman Ibrahim Mohammad, Asokan Vasudevan, Jasgurpreet Singh Chohan, Ahmed Fekry Salman, Manveet Singh, Ripendeep Singh, Pardeep Singh Bains, Parvoz Abdulkhakimov, Mohammad Ebrahim Astaneh, Narges Fereydouni
description: IntroductionMusculoskeletal disorders impose a substantial global disability burden. Conventional 3D bioprinting cannot replicate the dynamic, anisotropic architecture of bone, cartilage, skeletal muscle, and cardiac muscle. Four-dimensional (4D) bioprinting addresses this by integrating stimuli-responsive materials into constructs, enabling programmed shape transformation and adaptive behavior following implantation.

title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals the alteration of metabolites during the stewing process of Lueyang black-bone chicken meat
creator: Ling Wang, Guojin Li, Jie Gao, Jia Cheng, Zhengnan Yuan, Hongzhao Lu, Wenxian Zeng, Tao Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionBlack-bone chicken meat is rich in nutritional substances and bioactive compounds. Stewing is a traditional and healthy cooking style for black-bone chicken meat. However, the alteration of metabolites in chicken meat during stewing is still unknown.MethodsA comprehensive analysis of Lueyang black-bone chicken meat metabolites was performed in fresh chicken meat (FM), short-term heat-pretreated meat (PM), fully cooked meat (CM) and chicken soup (CS) via untargeted metabolomics.ResultsBy comparison, 200, 992 and 891 significantly differentially metabolites (DMs) were identified in the PM vs.

title: Development and External Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Automated Feedback Quality Assessment in Chinese Anesthesiology Residency Training
creator: Lifeng Yao, Yijun Chen, Jing Shen, Junge Zhang, Yiwei Zhang, Guojin Liang, Yiqin Ji
description: PurposeHigh-quality narrative feedback is essential for competency-based medical education, but manual evaluation of feedback is time-consuming and subjective. This research aims to develop and validate a machine learning (ML)-based model to automate the bulk evaluation of feedback quality from anesthesiology residency program instructors.

title: Crossing the blood-brain barrier: neurotrauma in disasters and resource-limited settings
creator: Michael J Anstadt, Tanya Egodage, Matthew J Martin, Purvi Pravinchandra Patel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryTraumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in natural disasters, armed conflict, and other resource-limited settings, where advanced imaging, invasive neuromonitoring, and specialized neurosurgical care, common in high-resource environments, are often unavailable. This narrative review summarizes the global health impact of TBI in austere conditions and outlines key management strategies and ethical considerations relevant to these contexts.

title: Longitudinal serological and virological survey of hepatitis E virus in wild boar (Sus scrofa majori, Maremman wild boar) and fallow deer (Dama dama) populations in a protected area of Central Italy
creator: Luca De Sabato, Mariagiovanna Domanico, Paola De Santis, Daniele Cecca, Giulia Bonella, Giovanni Mastrandrea, Roberta Onorati, Luigi Sorbara, Bianca Maria Varcasia, Barbara Franzetti, Andrea Caprioli, Antonio Battisti, Fabio Ostanello, Ilaria Di Bartolo
description: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is recognized as an emerging zoonosis. Pigs and wild boars are considered the main reservoirs of zoonotic HEV-3 and HEV-4 genotypes. In Europe, autochthonous human cases of hepatitis E, mainly associated with HEV-3 and consumption of raw or undercooked pig and wild boar liver/meat, have increased over the last decades.

title: Role of lymphadenectomy in advanced-stage ovarian cancer: a meta-analysis
creator: Carlo Ronsini, Francesca Pasanisi, Giada Andreoli, Pasquale De Franciscis, Luigi Cobellis, Giuseppe Vizzielli, Stefano Restaino, Paola Romeo, Vittorio Palmara, Stefano Cianci
description: BackgroundEpithelial Ovarian Cancer is one of the most lethal cancers among gynecologic malignancies. The disease metastasizes mainly through the peritoneal spread in the abdomen and through the lymphatic system. Lymph node involvement is present in 48% up to 75% of cases of advanced-stage ovarian cancer (ASOC).

title: Integrating AlphaFold2, RoseTTAFold2, and HADDOCK to refine Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) candidate selection: A case study with ZWINT
creator: Nora Abdelfattah, Bridget Broncales, Ivana Albert, Jaimee Kohan, Lei Yu
description: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) underpin most cellular processes, and disruptions to these interactions can lead to cellular dysfunction and disease. Understanding PPIs is essential for studying disease mechanisms, yet traditional experimental approaches are time- and labor-intensive. Recent advances in AI-based structural prediction tools, including AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold2, now enable efficient in silico exploration of potential PPIs.

title: Transitions and determinants of ICU-acquired frailty after critical illness: A multicenter cohort study using a multistate Markov model
creator: Tingting Wu, Yueqing Wei, Lan Shi, Rongjin Lin, Hong Li
description: BackgroundPreexisting frailty at ICU admission has been well investigated and linked to adverse outcomes, the continuum and determinants of new onset of frailty remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to estimate transition probabilities and intensities across non-frailty, frailty, and death after critical illness, and explore a set of potential variables associated with these transitions.

title: Characterizing headache patients admitted from the emergency department: a retrospective study
creator: Faisal AlGhamdi, Abdulelah A. Alzahrani, Khaleel I. Alwatyan, Reem A. Hariri, Abdullah A. Alhowaish, Rahaf F. Almobarak, Mohammed Almulhim, Faisal B. Alkhadra
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundHeadaches are a common complaint in emergency department (ED) presentations, but the demographics, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of patients admitted with headaches remain understudied. This retrospective study aims to investigate patients admitted with a chief complaint of headache.MethodsThe study examined the triage database of our ED from 01/01/2020 to 31/12/2022 to identify patients admitted to either the wards or intensive care unit (ICU) with headache as their primary complaint.ResultsOut of 347 identified patients, 100 met the inclusion criteria.

title: Time to return to sports in football players recovering from lower limb soft tissue injuries: a systematic review with meta-analysis
creator: Jente Wagemans, Elaheh Ahmadi, Jan Taeymans, Jeroen Van Eetvelt, Geert Van Neylen, Peter Catteeuw, Heiner Baur, Dirk Vissers
description: ObjectivesDepict football players’ average times to return to sports (RTS) after non-contact lower limb soft-tissue injuries.DesignSystematic review with meta-analysis.Data sourcesPubMed, WoS, Scopus, PEDro, Google Scholar and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled.Eligibility criteria for selecting studiesWe included records investigating time to return to sports in football players suffering from non-contact lower limb soft-tissue injuries.

title: Ultrasound-assisted hydrophobic deep eutectic solvent extraction and purification of ursolic acid and oleanolic acid from Cornus officinalis: Optimization and mechanistic insights
creator: Tengteng Yang, Chao Tan, Ruoliang Wang, Yixuan Shi, Junhai Liu, Yinku Liang, Chenyang Ren, Yongfei Wang, Yuan Yao
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical abstract

Introduction

Cornus officinalis, also referred to as red jujube bark and medicinal jujube, is widely distributed across China and is an important plant resource in the Qinba Mountains of Shaanxi Province [1]. Its fruit is rich in various bioactive substances, including cycloartenolides, triterpenic acids, flavonoids, polysaccharides, organic acid esters, and other bioactive components, giving it a substantial therapeutic value [2], [3]. Ursolic acid (UA) and oleanolic acid (OA), pentacyclic triterpenic acids, are isomeric compounds abundant in C.

title: The relationship between impostor phenomenon and career decision-making difficulties among nursing interns: the mediating role of psychological resilience
creator: Meina He, Yao Li, Hui Hu, Zuqiang Yu, Cong Cai, Yao Cheng, Lu Ma, Shanshan Liu
description: BackgroundIn the face of a global nursing shortage, nursing interns are crucial to sustaining the healthcare workforce. However, these interns encounter significant challenges in career decision-making, often exacerbated by the impostor phenomenon, which impedes their capacity to make informed choices.

title: Dixon Up-and-Down Method for Optimizing Oxycodone Dosage in Painless Colonoscopy
creator: Yujie Ding, Chunliu Hou, Yan Li
description: AimInadequate analgesia during painless colonoscopy can result in undesirable body movements, undermining patient safety and procedural success. Oxycodone, known for its dual κ- and μ-receptor agonism, may provide effective analgesia with a reduced incidence of adverse effects compared to other opioids. However, the optimal intravenous dose of oxycodone for suppressing body movement during colonoscopy has not been established.

title: The Prediction of Successful Aging by Frailty, Functional Cognition and Well-Being in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Survey
creator: Christos Kleisiaris, Theodora Arida, Maria Klesiora, Konstantinos Tsaras, Maria Malliarou, Ioanna V Papathanasiou, Theodosios Paralikas, Nikolaos Bakalis, Mahmoud Ogla Al-Hussami, Wafa Hamad Almegewly, Savvato Karavasileiadou, Theodore D Cosco
description: IntroductionIt is widely recognised that frailty components and the functional cognition are associated with successful aging (SA). However, the true figures of this association are uncertain.PurposeTo examine the prediction of SA by frailty, functional cognition and well-being in community-dwelling adults aged 65 years and over.

title: On the Use of Immunoglobulins for Pre-exposure Prophylaxis Against COVID-19 in Immunocompromised Patients
creator: Daniele Focosi, Massimo Franchini, Arturo Casadevall
description: COVID-19 remains a cause of significant mortality and morbidity for immunocompromised patients. In the current absence of effective monoclonal antibodies to SARS-CoV-2, standard commercial intravenous/subcutaneous immunoglobulin (IVIG/SCIG) lots provide an option for passive immunotherapy since these now consistently contain SARS-CoV-2-reactive antibodies.

title: Mediator role of psychological resilience between post-traumatic stress symptoms and burnout in academicians affected by the earthquakes in Türkiye
creator: Ayşegül Yetkin Tekin
description: PurposeThis study aims to investigate the mediator role of psychological resilience in the relationship between post-traumatic stress and burnout symptoms in academicians affected by two earthquakes that occurred on February 6, 2023, affecting 11 provinces of Türkiye.MethodsThe research sample consisted of 175 academicians affected by these earthquakes.

title: A Systematic and Narrative Review of Safety and Complications in Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery (MIGS) Between 2014–2024 [Letter]
creator: Zoltan Z Nagy, Kinga Kranitz, Iqbal Ike K Ahmed, Ticiana De Francesco, Eric Mikula, Tibor Juhasz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 14–2024.”1 While we acknowledge the authors’ commendable effort to synthesize safety data across a wide range of MIGS procedures, a material discrepancy between the manuscript body and Table 1 requires correction. In the text, the authors accurately describe the findings from our first-in-human 24-month FLIGHT study,2 noting that transient blood reflux into the anterior chamber was observed in 11 of 18 eyes (61.1%) on gonioscopy immediately after trabeculotomy creation, which resolved by postoperative day one and had no impact on vision.

title: “No one talks about it”: using emotional methodologies to overcome climate silence and inertia in Higher Education
creator: Anna Pigott, Hanna Nuuttila, Merryn Thomas, Fern Smith, Kirsti Bohata, Tavi Murray, Marega Palser, Emily Holmes, Osian Elias
description: Higher Education (HE) is, at best, struggling to rise to the challenges of the climate and ecological crises (CEC) and, at worst, actively contributing to them by perpetuating particular ways of knowing, relating, and acting. Calls for HE to radically transform its activities in response to the polycrises abound, yet questions about how this will be achieved are often overlooked.

title: Association Between Pneumonia Risk and Anticholinergic Burden Among Patients with Different Frailty Levels [Response to Letter]
creator: Avery Shuei-He Yang, Hsin-Yu Fan Chiang, Daniel Hsiang-Te Tsai, Albert Tzu-Ming Chuang, Edward Chia-Cheng Lai
description: al analyses based on those comments in the following contents. Cognitive dysfunction and psychiatric disorders represented important factors in clinical practice. Patients with cognitive dysfunction and psychiatric disorders are at increased risk of pneumonia through multiple mechanisms, including impaired swallowing and airway protection, functional decline, and immune dysregulation.

title: Lived experience of being a grandparent in one region of Spain: a qualitative study
creator: Sofia García-Sanjuán, Ana Isabel Gutiérrez-García, María José Cabañero-Martínez, Manuel Fernández-Alcántara, Maria del Carmen Rocamora-Rodriguez, Silvia Escribano
description: BackgroundThe evolution of the family model in Europe in the 21st century, and particularly in Spain, has led to grandparents playing a major role in caring for their grandchildren. Grandparents are required to take on certain functions and roles in order to provide this care.

title: Level of Emergency Preparedness and Associated Barriers at the Accident and Emergency Ward of a LMIC Hospital: A Cross-Sectional Assessment Using the WHO HEAT Tool
creator: Joel Nabeshya, Elizabeth Atiang, Charity Kwarikunda, Rachel Luwaga, Vallence Niyonzima
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEmergency preparedness is a challenge for hospital emergency departments (EDs). In the USA, over 68% of 983 EDs were not emergency prepared, while in Ghana, one hospital’s emergency preparedness level was only 57.4%.

title: Association between the LDL/HDL ratio and sarcopenia in Chinese community-dwelling older adults
creator: Shanshan Lu, Cheng Wu, Yushuang Lin, Zhengkai Shen, Xiang Lu
description: ObjectivesThe link between lipid disorders and diverse diseases is amply documented. Yet, research probing how serum lipid levels tie in with sarcopenia remains scarce. This study delves into the connection between the LDL/HDL ratio and sarcopenia among elderly Chinese people.MethodsA total of 3,968 senior participants from Chinese communities were included in this cross-sectional study.

title: ESTRO-EPTN guidelines for independent dose calculation and log file-based patient-specific quality assurance in scanned particle therapy
creator: Loïc Grevillot, Oliver Jäkel, Abdallah Qubala, Julian Horn, Adam H. Aitkenhead, Xiaoying Liang, Giuseppe Magro, Klará Badraoui-Čuprová, Jan Vilimovský, Jörg Wulff, Katrin Henkner, Catharine H. Clark, Damir Skrijelj, Ilaria Rinaldi, Kevin Souris, Séverine Rossomme, Franciska Lebbink, Liu Hong, Dawid
description: Background and Purpose: Independent dose calculation (IDC) and log file-based patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) are increasingly used in scanned particle therapy (PT) to address pitfalls of phantom-based verifications. Highly modulated treatment fields, steep dose gradients, and growing interest for adaptive treatments require quality assurance (QA) approaches that are cost effective, patient-specific, and closely linked to the delivered treatment.

title: Genome-wide identification and expression profiling of GATA gene family in response to salt stress in sesame (Sesamum indicum L.)
creator: Sk Shoaibur Rahaman, Jibon Chandro Roy, Khandker Shazia Afrin, Nasar Uddin Ahmed, Md Abdur Rahim
description: GATA transcription factors (TFs) are characterized by the existence of a type IV zinc-fingered structure. This TF family plays a significant role in growth and development, and in response to abiotic and biotic stresses. The GATA gene family has been well characterized in various plant species but remains unexplored to date in sesame (Sesamum indicum L.).

title: Antibody-dependent priming of spontaneous germinal centers by autoreactive B cells
creator: Danny Kim, Kristy Chiang, Andrea D. Largent, Ragan A. Pitner, Sivasankaran Munusamy Ponnan, Brock J. McKinney, Richard G. James, David J. Rawlings, Shaun W. Jackson
description: Autoreactive germinal centers (GCs) are central to autoimmune pathogenesis, yet the mechanisms by which single autoreactive B cell clones prime systemic autoimmunity remain unclear. Using the 564Igi mixed chimera model, we demonstrate that autoreactive 564Igi B cells break tolerance in wild-type B cells through an unexpected mechanism independent of cognate T cell interactions.

title: MAPT regulates autophagic-lysosomal function and phagocytosis in human microglia
creator: Kylie J. Schache, Rui Zhang, Audrey E. Street, Emma Starr, Jacob A. Marsh, David J. Kast, Sally Temple, Abhirami K. Iyer, Celeste M. Karch
description: Tauopathies are characterized by the accumulation and spread of pathogenic tau aggregates throughout the brain, a process that is increasingly recognized to involve not only neurons but also microglia. However, whether pathogenic MAPT directly alters microglial degradative capacity remains poorly understood.

title: Feature-based valuation and its impairment in people with compulsive and addictive symptoms
creator: Morgan G. Moll, Ryan K. Read, Thomas W. Elston
description: Effective decision-making requires evaluating options based on relevant features while reducing attention to those that are not. However, how attention prioritizes one source of information over another during value-based decisions remains unknown. Across 7 experiments, we show that irrelevant features both constructively and destructively interfered with how values are assigned to choice options.

title: Extracellular Vacuole-derived bodies (EVacs) mediate RNA secretion in plants
creator: M. Lucía Borniego, Meenu Singla-Rastogi, Megha H. Sampangi-Ramaiah, Ang-Yu Liu, Giovanni Gonzalez-Gutierrez, Sarah J. Cox-Vázquez, Chi-Tam Vo, Akihito Fukudome, Ricardo Javier Vázquez, Blake C. Meyers, Patricia Baldrich, Roger W. Innes
description: Extracellular RNAs are found in the plant extracellular space, but how they are exported from cells remains unclear. We found that the plant vacuole is a major source of extracellular RNA and identified a class of large e xtracellular vac uole-derived bodies, which we termed EVacs, that are key mediators of this transport.

title: Designing antimicrobials with programmable mechanism and safety
creator: Paulina Szymczak, Marcelo D.T. Torres, Diogo Soares, Leon Hetzel, Bruno Puczko-Szymański, Stefanie Jegelka, Stephan Günnemann, Fabian J. Theis, Cesar de la Fuente-Nunez, Ewa Szczurek
description: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are a promising solution to antimicrobial resistance, yet generative models for their design cannot control the physicochemical properties and motifs that shape activity and selectivity. Here, we present OmegAMP, a conditional diffusion framework controlling net charge, mean hydrophobicity, and sequence length, supporting de novo, analog, and motif-guided design.

title: Guided tissue regeneration for severe periodontal disease in dogs: A retrospective study
creator: Chul Park, Md. Mahbubur Rahman, Kwangil Han, Inseong Jeong, Namsoo Kim
description: Clinical evidence on guided tissue regeneration (GTR) in dogs with advanced periodontal defects is limited. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes and tooth survival after GTR in dogs with severe periodontal disease. The medical records of 67 dogs with 129 treated teeth/sites in total were reviewed.

title: Leveraging social media for youth engagement in HIV prevention: evaluation of the Y-FIT GH open-call campaign in Ghana
creator: Gloria Aidoo-Frimpong, Senam Aku Biddah, Maame Araba Oduro, Abass Tando Abubakar, Yaa Adutwumwaa Obeng, Dorcas Adom, Winfred Kofi Mensah, Brian Ankrah, Daniel Selase Anyidoho, Paul Sowah, Ernest Ortsin, Stephen Ayisi-Addo, Caroline Kingori, Juliet Iwelunmor
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Adolescents and young adults (AYA) in Ghana continue to experience barriers to HIV prevention, including stigma, limited awareness of HIV self-testing and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and insufficient access to AYA-friendly prevention services. This descriptive process evaluation examined how a 2-month, multi-platform communication strategy supported participation in the Youth-Friendly Innovation Tools for HIV Prevention in Ghana national open call for creative HIV self-testing and oral and long-acting PrEP advocacy ideas. The strategy combined paid Facebook advertising, LinkedIn dissemination, and peer-to-peer WhatsApp sharing.

title: VizChemoton: Visualization of Quantum Chemical Reaction Networks and Their Cheminformatics Features
creator: Enric Petrus, Diego Garay-Ruiz, Thomas Weymuth, Markus Reiher, Thomas B. Hofstetter
description: Automated explorations of chemical reaction networks (CRNs) guided by quantum chemistry (QC) calculations are undergoing rapid development that enables numerous applications. However, CRNs are accessible primarily through specialized quantum chemistry software without interface for cheminformatic exploitation of the generated data. Here, we present VizChemoton, an open-source module within the reaction exploration framework Software for Chemical Interaction Networks (SCINE).

title: Efficient Discovery of Potent AKR1B10 Inhibitors Using Co-folding Model Boltz‑2
creator: Shinya Kawano, Akira Ikari, Satoshi Endo, Kentaro Tomii
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Although affinity prediction of protein–ligand binding remains an important challenge, cofolding models are expected to make virtual screening more effective for drug discovery and development. To verify the effectiveness of selecting a tractable number of candidates from a compound library using cofolding models, we strove to identify a novel inhibitory active compound using Boltz-2, a representative cofolding model, for aldo-keto reductase 1B10 (AKR1B10), which is highly expressed in various cancers.

title: FMM-AutoOpt: A Python Tool for Automated GROMACS FMM Parameter Optimization
creator: Louise J. Persson, Erik G. Marklund
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The fast multipole method (FMM) for computing Coulombic forces in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations offers benefits for a variety of systems, including nonperiodic configurations such as molecules in vacuum and large-scale systems where many other approaches encounter limitations. Because FMM parameters govern both simulation accuracy and computational performance, and because the optimal solution is highly system-dependent, we have developed FMM-AutoOpt for the automated benchmarking of FMM parameters with GROMACS. Relying solely on standard Python libraries and GROMACS FMM ( KohnkeB., J.

title: Survival impact of involvement of lymph node stations 16b1, 9, and 8a during pancreatoduodenectomy for pancreatic and periampullary cancers (PANODE): prospective multicentre study
creator: J Annelie Suurmeijer, Bobby K Pranger, Leonard W F Seelen, Mahsoem Ali, L Bengt van Rijssen, Dorine S Tseng, Tara M Mackay, Jacob L van Dam, Hjalmar C van Santvoort, Bas Groot Koerkamp, Arantza Farina Sarasqueta, Casper H van Eijck, Mike S L Liem, Geert Kazemier, Vincent B Nieuwenhuijs, Ignace H de
description: BackgroundCurrent guidelines do not recommend routine sampling of lymph node stations (LNS) 16b1, 9, and 8a during pancreatoduodenectomy for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and other periampullary cancers because prospective multicentre studies are lacking. This study evaluated the association between the involvement of these LNS and overall survival (OS).

title: Australian women’s perspectives on gendered vulnerability, commercial power, and resistance to the commercialization of menopause
creator: Samantha L Thomas, Simone McCarthy, Hannah Pitt, Katrina Wood, Tina D Purnat, Sarah L White, Martha Hickey
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A range of commercial actors actively shape how menopause is understood, experienced, and managed. While existing research highlights concerns about commercial influence, much less is known about how women themselves interpret, negotiate, and respond to these commercialized menopause environments. Using an online qualitative survey, this study explored the opinions of n = 362 Australian cisgender women (45–64 years) about the commercialization of menopause. Data were interpreted using a reflexive approach to thematic analysis, with three themes constructed from the data.

title: A First Case of Compulsive Amnestic Sleep-Related Shopping Induced by Pramipexole Therapy of Restless Legs Syndrome
creator: Michael Todd, Carlos H. Schenck, Erin Golden, Ranji Varghese
description: Dopamine receptor agonists (DAs) such as pramipexole/ropinirole are recognized treatments for restless legs syndrome (RLS) and Parkinson's disease (PD). It is well established that these medications can cause impulse control disorders (ICDs) during wakefulness, side effects with serious and potentially life-altering consequences. Impulse control disorders are recurrent difficult-to-resist behaviors that can be harmful to the patient or others around them.

title: 대한영상의학회지 심사위원님들께 드리는 감사의 글
creator: 성헌 김
description: 김동준 (연세의대 세브란스병원) 김민욱 (서울특별시보라매병원) 김보현 (가톨릭대학교 서울성모병원) 김성준 (연세의대 강남세브란스병원) 김성헌 (가톨릭대학교 서울성모병원) 김수진 (중앙대학교병원) 김여주 (한양대학교의료원) 김영진 (연세대학교) 김유리 (원광대학교병원) 김은희 (이대목동병원) 김재현 (서울대학교병원) 김정례 (우리아이들병원) 김지나 (강북삼성병원) 김지민 (가톨릭대학교 은평성모병원) 김지영 (분당서울대학교병원) 김지은 (경상국립대학교병원) 김진우 (연세원주기독병원) 김진유 (부산대학교병원) 김진혁 (양산부산대학교병원) 김찬교 (성균관대학교 삼성서울병원) 김채리 (고려대학교 안산병원) 김초희 (성균관대학교 삼성서울병원) 김택민 (서울대학교병원) 김현주 (순천향대학교병원) 김현지 (가톨릭대학교 은평성모병원) 김현철

title: Three-dimensional deep learning nomogram for post-plan quality assurance in high-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy☆
creator: Joel Beaudry, Tonghe Wang, Shirin A. Enger, Antonio L. Damato
description: PurposeClassical nomograms for high-dose-rate (HDR) prostate brachytherapy quality assurance (QA) evaluate agreement between planned and expected total dwell time but do not directly assess the three-dimensional treated volume. This study's aim was to develop a deep learning-based 3D nomogram to predict institution-specific clinical 100% isodose volumes from anatomy and dwell positions for post-plan QA.

title: Metabolomics workbench: data-driven classification and correlation analysis between metabolite classes, biomarkers, and drugs
creator: Mikhail M Khandokhin, Aleksandr Sokolov, Nikolay Oskolkov, Robert Fredriksson, Olga E Titova, Helgi B Schiöth
description: Public repositories now accumulate an unprecedented amount of metabolomics data. Despite the opportunities for large-scale meta-analyses opened by these repositories, the deposited data rarely becomes systematically re-analyzed. We conducted a systematic metadata-based re-analysis of all human blood metabolomics studies in the Metabolomics Workbench performed using Orbitrap or QTOF mass spectrometry, encompassing 44 165 samples.

title: Response to Khodamoradi: Methodological clarifications regarding NanOx predictions in helium SOBP
creator: Thomas Berger, Gersende Alphonse, Mario Alcocer-Avila, Caterina Monini, Charbel Koumeir, Claire Rodriguez-Lafrasse, Nicolas Varmenot, Vincent Métivier, Ferid Haddad, Jean Michel Létang, Étienne Testa
description: w, both criticisms are based, at least in part, on misunderstandings of our methodology. Khodamoradi's first concern relates to the use of SQ20B data for tuning the NanOx model and the subsequent use of the tuned model to predict survival in the same cell line.

title: Combined Day–Night Heat Damage in Soybean Is Driven by Nighttime Warming
creator: Gabriel Ferraz Guimarães, Jéssica de Jesus Santos, Rafael Vasconcelos Ribeiro, Milton Costa Lima Neto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Asymmetric warming, characterized by faster increases in nighttime than daytime temperatures, is an emerging threat to crop performance. However, the interactive physiological effects of day versus night heat remain insufficiently resolved in soybean ( Glycine max L. Here, we evaluated soybean responses to 4 day/night thermal regimes (28°C/22°C, 40°C/22°C, 28°C/28°C, and 40°C/28°C) to test whether nighttime warming is the dominant driver of stress disruption. Isolated daytime heat (40°C/22°C) enhanced photosynthetic performance and maintained biomass, indicating short‐term functional plasticity.

title: ‘It Makes Me Feel Confident’: A Community Based Participatory Study of Experiences of Employment for People With Intellectual Disabilities
creator: Deanna Gallichan, Chloe Deacon, Karen Gresty, Simon Rundle
description: BackgroundA social enterprise brewery requested help from researchers to understand their employment opportunities for people with intellectual disabilities (‘trainees’). A community‐based participatory framework (CBPR) was used to develop the research.MethodDigital storytelling was selected to enable trainees to express their views about their work. Six participants created digital stories with support from researchers.

title: Biosolids in Washington State: Putting per‐ and poly‐fluorinated alkyl substances concerns into a real‐world context
creator: Sally Brown, Scott Mansell
description: Washington State has a history of beneficial use of municipal biosolids. The Department of Ecology recently conducted a voluntary survey of per‐ and poly‐fluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS) in biosolids. Results of that survey are presented and compared with the results from mandatory sampling in Michigan.

title: The forgotten organ: Why the oral microbiome belongs in every physician's toolkit
creator: Victoria Sampson
description: The oral cavity is the most densely colonised microbial niche in the human body after the gut – over 700 species and an estimated two billion bacteria (Deo and Deshmukh, 2019) – yet it remains conspicuously absent from the systemic health conversation.

title: The hidden consequences of marine heatwaves: rising Vibrio risk in European coastal waters
creator: Jan C Semenza, Joaquin A Trinanes, Jaime Martinez-Urtaza
description: heatwaves dominate public attention, because of their immediate impacts on human health, they often overshadow equally profound changes occurring in the oceans. During the same month, the western Mediterranean Sea and adjacent Atlantic coastal waters experienced a record-breaking marine heatwave.

title: Decoupling Transparency and Electron Injection in Ultrathin Ag Electrodes Using an Al/MoO3 Double Seed Layer for Transparent Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
creator: Yeyun Bae, Kyoungeun Lee, Kyunghoon Lee, Jaeyeop Lee, Jiyoon Oh, Jiwoong Yang, Chansu Kim, Jeongkyun Roh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). There is growing interest in transparent quantum dot light‐emitting diodes (Tr‐QLEDs) for window‐type displays. For such devices, the top transparent electrode must simultaneously provide high optical transmittance, low sheet resistance, and efficient charge injection. Ultrathin Ag films are promising because of their high conductivity and transparency, but they tend to grow via the Volmer–Weber mode, resulting in poor continuity and increased resistance.

title: Surrogate Scattering Matrix‐Guided Inverse Design of Nanophotonic Neural Networks
creator: Azka Maula Iskandar Muda, Uğur Teğin
description: Optical computing offers a route to address the growing computational demands of machine learning, with inverse‐designed nanophotonic media providing a compact path to passive optical operators. Training such devices end to end remains expensive because each geometry update requires full‐wave forward and adjoint evaluations. We introduce a surrogate‐guided inverse‐design framework that separates task learning from electromagnetic realization.

title: The FHJ debate: Dental health is so crucial that it should be in the medical school curriculum
creator: Jasmine Ho, Clarissa Hjalmarsson
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This debate article evaluates whether dental health education should be more widely integrated into the undergraduate medical curriculum. The authors present evidence-informed arguments situated within an evolving landscape of healthcare delivery, professional expectations, and political system-level pressures. Central to both perspectives is the need to advocate for patients’ best interests, along with the practicalities of implementing an integrated, cross-disciplinary healthcare curriculum.

title: Antioxidant therapy, N-acetyl-L-cysteine, effects on pancreatic β cells: therapeutic promise or potential harm?
creator: Meg Schuurman, Jonathan Nguyen, Malina Barillaro, Nica Borradaile, Rennian Wang
description: N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) is a widely used antioxidant with increasing public interest in its use for treating metabolic disease, yet its effects on pancreatic β cells remain incompletely understood. Most studies focus on NAC's benefits under pathological conditions—such as obesity, high-fat diet exposure, and type 2 diabetes—where oxidative stress impairs β-cell function, identity, and survival.

title: Neurofilaments support the differentiation of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis from degenerative cervical myelopathy
creator: Julia Goebell, Franziska Bachhuber, Jutta Karmann, Veronika Klose, Jan Kassubek, Hans-Peter Müller, Hayrettin Tumani, Albert Ludolph
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The differential diagnosis between degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and early amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is often clinically challenging; laboratory tests that support this distinction could be highly valuable. This study examined the concentrations of neurofilament light chain (NfL) and the phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNfH), in CSF and serum of carefully selected patients with DCM, spinal canal stenosis (SCS) and ALS, after exclusion of major neurological confounders. Patients were assigned to five groups according to MRI findings and ALS diagnosis.

title: Risk of atrial fibrillation according to electrocardiographic risk factors: a nationwide cohort study of 1.5 million patients
creator: Casper Binding, Christoffer Polcwiartek, Kristian Kragholm, Sam Riahi, Mikkel Porsborg Andersen, Helle Collatz Christensen, Mohamad Hassan El-Chouli, Signe Juul Riddersholm, Lise Da Riis-Vestergaard, Peter Søgaard, Gregory Y H Lip, Christian Torp-Pedersen, Daniel Friedman, Anders Nissen Bonde, Claus
description: AimsAtrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with an increased risk of stroke, yet no evidence exists on the collective effect of electrocardiogram (ECG) risk factors in early detection of AF. We aimed to evaluate the risk of new-onset AF and stroke according to specific ECG risk factors to identify patients at high risk of developing AF.

title: Targeting calciphylaxis: the emergence of vitamin K as a potential treatment
creator: Maria Fusaro, Smeeta Sinha, Antonio Bellasi, Markus Ketteler, Carlo Alfieri, Martin H de Borst, Ditte Hansen, Pietro Manuel Ferraro, Juan Miguel Díaz-Tocados, Mathias Haarhaus, Mehmet Kanbay, Maurizio Gallieni, Paolo Simioni, Sandro Giannini, Sharon Huish, Althea Cossettini
description: Calciphylaxis, or calcific uraemic arteriolopathy, is a rare, life-threatening vascular disorder predominantly affecting patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), especially those on dialysis. It is characterized by arteriolar calcification, thrombosis, and painful ischemic skin lesions that frequently ulcerate, contributing to high morbidity and mortality. Calciphylaxis arises from medial arterial calcification, endothelial injury, and a pro-inflammatory, pro-thrombotic milieu.

title: Interventional radiation immune-boosting (iRIB). The role of concomitant interventional radiotherapy (modern brachytherapy) in immunotherapy: A hypothesis-generating systematic review
creator: Roberta Muni, Valentina Lancellotta, Bruno Fionda, Enrico Rosa, Piotr Wojcieszek, Roberto Iacovelli, Monica Mangoni, Gabriella Macchia, Alessio Giuseppe Morganti, Maria Antonietta Gambacorta, Roberto Iezzi, Luca Tagliaferri
description: PurposeSynergistic activity of radiation and immunotherapy is well known to the extent that it can be referred to as radiation immuno-boosting. Interventional radiotherapy (IRT; modern brachytherapy) has a potential immunomodulatory advantage compared with external beam radiotherapy due to highly conformal dose distribution and dose heterogeneity, engaging multiple immunogenic mechanisms with distinct dose-response profiles.

title: From detection to action: Transparency, accuracy, and integration for clinical artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal aging
creator: Ta-Wei Tai, Dung Van Tran
description: trates how AI can extract additional clinical information from images obtained during routine care, enabling earlier identification of individuals who might otherwise remain unscreened. AI may accelerate screening, automate selected screening tasks, extend clinical capacity, and support case finding in regions where dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and trained personnel are limited.

title: KAT-Net: a hyperbolic routing framework for joint lysine acylation site prediction with shared sequence–structure representations
creator: Hao Wu, Yiyu Lin, Lun Zhu, Yan Wang, Shan Chang, Sen Yang
description: Protein lysine acylation regulates protein function through changes in local chemistry, structure, and molecular interactions. Acetylation (Kac), succinylation (Ksucc), and crotonylation (Kcr) share the lysine centre but differ in acyl-group chemistry, motivating joint yet task-aware prediction. We developed KAT-Net, a multi-task framework integrating ESM-2 representations, physicochemical priors, and AlphaFold2-derived structural context.

title: Epidemiology, risk factors and clinical outcome of community-acquired pneumonia in severely immunosuppressed patients: a comprehensive analysis from the multinational, prospective CAPNETZ Cohort
creator: Stephanie Müller, Gopinath Krishnamoorthy, Grit Barten-Neiner, Gernot Rohde, Mathias W. Pletz, Jessica Rademacher, Jan Rupp, Martin Witzenrath, Andreas Essig, Paul Schmidt, Marcus Panning, Benjamin Thomas Schleenvoigt, Martin Kolditz, M. Dreher, M. Dreher, C. Cornelissen, W. Knüppel, D. Stolz, N. Su
description: PurposeDespite growing evidence that immunosuppression (IS) influences aetiology and prognosis of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), there remains a lack of data from representative multicentre studies.MethodsThe multinational prospective CAPNETZ study includes patients with CAP and HIV since 2017, and with other causes of IS since 2020.

title: Characterizing the credentialed bachelor's-level behavioral health support workforce: a national descriptive study
creator: Brianna M Lombardi, Lisa D Zerden, Maria Gaiser
description: IntroductionPersistent shortages of the behavioral health workforce have prompted interest in expanding roles for bachelor's-level behavioral health support workers as a strategy for increasing care. States vary in how they regulate this workforce. This study characterized how US states define the bachelor's-level behavioral health workforce through credentialing structures, educational requirements, and scope of practice.

title: A collaborative hybrid network with aggregated attention for pulmonary nodule detection
creator: Jianle Chen, Jianyu Zhu, Yiying Wang, Yuyan Lin, Huilian Liao
description: BackgroundLung cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection for improving patient survival. Current imaging‑based methods for pulmonary nodule (PN) detection are often limited by low efficiency and suboptimal accuracy, falling short of the demands for precise clinical diagnosis.

title: Effects of morning versus evening high-intensity exercise on electroencephalographic and autonomic responses in middle-aged women
creator: Jae-Myun Ko, Wi-Young So, Jae-Hyun Jung
description: [Purpose] The time of day at which exercise is performed influences physiological responses and performance, and thus its health benefits. This study investigated whether electroencephalographic (EEG) and autonomic nervous system responses to morning versus evening exercise differed in middle-aged women.[Methods] Thirty women aged 50-60 years were randomly assigned to a morning or evening exercise group.

title: Human–artificial intelligence collaboration in emergency medical services: from diagnostic algorithms to shared decision support
creator: Hang A Park
description: ance comparable to, and in some cases better than, conventional methods [3]. AI-assisted ECG interpretation has reduced inappropriate catheterization laboratory activations, and retrieval-augmented large language models have shown potential for improving the consistency of prehospital triage [4–6]. Natural language processing has also been used in emergency dispatch calls to support earlier recognition of time-critical conditions, including out-of-hospital cardiac arrest [2].

title: A complementary amino acid formulation enhances exercise-induced skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training
creator: Deunsol Hwang, Sunghwan Kyun, Inkwon Jang, Taeho Kim, Nayeon Kim, Jungyong Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Insu Kwon, Ahjin Kim, Hangsu Cho, Taehyeon Park, Soohan Jung, Jisu Kim, Kiwon Lim
description: [Purpose] This study investigated whether a five-amino-acid formulation integrating complementary anabolic, metabolic, and redox-supporting functions enhances skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training.[Methods] Male C57BL/6N mice were assigned to eight groups receiving vehicle, leucine (300 mg/kg), or amino acid formulation (150-1,500 mg/kg). All mice completed four weeks of ladder resistance training, while the assigned supplements were administered orally once daily.

title: Effects of keiser-assisted Nordic hamstring curl training on hamstring flexibility, mechanical properties, and pitching performance in high school baseball pitchers
creator: Ye-Jun Han, Hyun Ahn, Sea-Hyun Bae, Kyung-Yoon Kim
description: [Purpose] This study aimed to investigate the effects of 10-week Keiser-assisted Nordic hamstring curl (NHC) training on the mechanical properties, muscle strength, and flexibility of the hamstrings, as well as shoulder range of motion (ROM) and pitching performance in high school baseball pitchers.[Methods] Sixteen high school baseball pitchers performed Keiser assisted NHC training for 10 weeks.

title: Effects of a low-protein, high-fructose corn syrup diet on skeletal muscle and bone in young adult mice: a pilot study
creator: Hyerim Park
description: [Purpose] This study aimed to examine the effects of chronic consumption of a low-protein diet combined with 10% high-fructose corn syrup (HFCS) on skeletal muscle and bone health in mice. [Methods] Seven-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were fed either a normal diet or a low-protein diet supplemented with 10% HFCS for 12 weeks.

title: Analysis of Postoperative Quality of Life in Patients With Acute Type A Aortic Dissection After Extensive Arch Repair via Partial Upper Sternotomy
creator: Linfeng Xie, Xiujuan Wang, Zhaofeng Zhang, Debin Jiang, Xinfan Lin
description: Background:This study aimed to compare health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with acute type A aortic dissection (AAAD) who underwent extensive arch repair via partial upper sternotomy (PUS) or full median sternotomy (FS).Methods:Data were collected from 112 patients with AAAD who were divided into two groups based on the surgical approach.

title: Early Initiation of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: Efficacy, Safety, and Implementation in Stabilized Patients
creator: Alfredo Mauriello, Adriana Correra, Anna Chiara Maratea, Valeria Cetoretta, Francesco Giallauria, Giovanni Esposito, Alfonso Desiderio, Francesco Sabatella, Renato Gioia, Gemma Marrazzo, Biagio Liccardo, Vincenzo Russo, Paolo Trambaiolo, Antonello D’Andrea
description: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have fundamentally reshaped the pharmacological management of chronic heart failure (HF). However, the role of these inhibitors during the vulnerable phase of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) has historically been limited by concerns regarding hemodynamic stability and renal function.

title: Population-based registry analysis of cervical cancer trends in Tashkent, Uzbekistan 2014-2024
creator: Ulugbek Khudayberdievich Mirzaev, Jasur Ravshanovich Juraev, Iroda Pulatovna Sharipova, Sarvar Temurovich Islomov, Nodira Isroilovna Tursunova, Sitora Rakhmatova, Fatima Shokir Qizi Shodieva, Mirzarakhim Mirzakhakimovich Baynazarov, Khasanjon Kobiljon Ugli Odilov, Dilbar Yuldashevna Yuldasheva, Goli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCervical cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women in Uzbekistan, exceeding WHO elimination targets. Despite a school-based HPV vaccination program launched in 2019, screening coverage remains low, leading to delayed diagnoses; we examined cervical cancer trends in Tashkent (2014-2024) to evaluate the impact of the Korea Foundation for International Healthcare (KOFIH) screening project and UNFPA/UNDP HPV testing initiatives.MethodsWe analyzed Tashkent City Oncoregister data for women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer or carcinoma in situ (CIS) between 2014 and

title: Comparative evaluation of pyrolysis oils derived from lignocellulosic biomass and municipal solid waste as potential bitumen modifiers
creator: Bhaswati Bora, Nikhil Saboo, Praveen Kumar, Sonal K. Thengane
description: The transition toward sustainable road construction has led to increased research on replacing conventional asphalt binders with bio-based and waste-derived alternatives. Bio-bitumen derived from lignocellulosic biomass and binders modified using domestic and industrial waste have shown significant potential in reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by up to 80%. Life cycle assessments have reported net-negative emissions for certain biomass-based binders.

title: Nitrogen fertilization outweighs plant species loss in shaping bacterial belowground diversity in an alpine meadow on the central Tibetan Plateau
creator: Dongmei Wu, CiRen Quzong, Zhongjun Jia, Antje Schwalb, Georg Guggenberger, Shiping Wang, Tsechoe Dorji, Michael Pester
description: Plant species loss and nitrogen fertilization affect grassland biodiversity. However, their interactive effects on plant communities, soil properties, and the soil microbiome remain insufficiently understood. We analysed how the removal of plant species, with and without urea addition, influenced plant diversity, soil properties, and soil bacterial communities in a Tibetan Plateau grassland.

title: Making Antibiotic Guidance Work in the Emergency Department
creator: Hae Suk Cheong
description: need more antibiotic knowledge [2]. Existing guidance is often designed in a form that does not match the work of emergency care [1,3]. The authors conducted focus group interviews with 16 physicians involved in antibiotic prescribing at four tertiary hospitals in Korea.

title: Bacteriophage-Antibiotic Combinations in the Era of Antimicrobial Resistance
creator: Shinwon Lee
description: es carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales among the critical-priority pathogens for research and development, together with other major resistant organisms that continue to threaten contemporary clinical practice [1]. Against this background, bacteriophage (or phage) therapy has re-emerged as a potential therapeutic option for difficult-to-treat bacterial infections, including those for which effective antibiotic options are limited, and as an adjunct to conventional therapy.

title: Synergistic Effect of Bacteriophage vB_KpnS_Pey and Antibiotic Combinations against Clinical Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates
creator: Parva Farmehr, Salehe Sabouri, Roya Ahmadrajabi, Saereh Mohammadpour, Hossein Hosseini-Nave, Sanaz Rastegar
description: BackgroundThe global rise of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP), presents a serious therapeutic challenge. This study aimed to isolate and characterize a bacteriophage effective against prophage-free CRKP and to evaluate its potential synergistic effects with ciprofloxacin, meropenem, gentamicin, and colistin.

title: Integrated RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies NRXN1+ Cell-Fibroblast Associated MAPK Signaling in Prurigo Nodularis
creator: Jiyun Jang, Young-Bok Lee, Hwee-Seon Park, Narang Hong, Hyung Don Kook, Hye Jung Jung, Jong-Il Kim, Jiyoung Ahn
description: PurposePrurigo nodularis (PN) is chronic pruritic dermatosis with hyperkeratotic nodules and persistent itch, occurring alone or with atopic dermatitis (AD). The molecular basis of nodular architecture and sustained pruritus remain poorly defined, particularly the role of fibroblasts and their interactions with neuronal components.

title: Association Between C-Reactive Protein-Triglyceride Glucose Index and All-Cause Mortality and Exacerbation in Adult Asthma: NHANES, 1999–2010 and 2015–2018
creator: Jiaye Wang, Miaomiao Zhao, Hao Chen, Shiyu Hu, Chengshui Chen, Yingqing Zhang, Wenyu Chen
description: PurposeThis study investigates the association between the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), indicative of systemic inflammation and insulin resistance, and all-cause mortality as well as asthma exacerbations in adults with asthma.MethodsData from eight cycles of the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (1999–2010 and 2015–2018) were analyzed.

title: Psychotropic drugs in drinking water? A scoping review of evidence on diazepam and fluoxetine
creator: Paula Pinheiro Teixeira, Beatriz Assunção Pereira, Roberta da Silva Carneiro, Lara Júlia Moraes de Assis, Mariana Luiza Leal, Matheus Marcon
description: The global prevalence of mental disorders has increased considerably in recent decades. This evidence, associated with population growth and the expansion of access to medications, favors the growing global consumption of psychotropic drugs. Consequently, an increasing load of these substances is introduced into the environment, especially into water bodies, characterizing them as emerging contaminants.

title: Invasive alien plants in riparian ecosystems: a study from two lowland rivers in Eastern Poland
creator: Joanna Sender, Monika Różańska-Boczula
description: Riparian ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots but are also highly vulnerable to biological invasions due to strong hydrological connectivity, recurrent disturbance and exposure to nutrient inputs. This study examined patterns of invasive alien plant species (IAS) occurrence along two lowland rivers in eastern Poland (the Biala Lada and Czarna Lada).

title: InstructPLM-mu: protein fitness prediction from structure instructions
creator: Junde Xu, Yapin Shi, Lijun Lang, Taoyong Cui, Zhiming Zhang, Guangyong Chen, Jiezhong Qiu, Pheng-Ann Heng
description: Multimodal protein language models (PLMs) deliver strong performance on mutation-effect prediction, but training such models from scratch demands substantial computational resources. In this paper, we propose a fine-tuning framework called InstructPLM-mu and investigate the question: Can a pretrained sequence-only PLM, augmented with structural information during fine-tuning, match the performance of end-to-end trained multimodal models?

title: Therapeutic vaccines for NSCLC: From mechanisms to clinical translation
creator: Weijing Liu, Jiefei Han, Kailun Fei, Yiting Dong, Man Li, Jie Zhao, Mingzhao Wang, Zhuoran Li, Siyuan Chen, Jiachen Xu, Amit Jain
description: Despite advances in targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), durable disease control remains elusive for most patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly those with advanced-stage disease. Therapeutic cancer vaccines offer the potential for sustained immune surveillance by inducing tumor-specific effector and memory T-cell responses. However, their clinical benefits have been inconsistent to date.

title: GDF-15 and immune resistance: A new frontier in non-small cell lung cancer immunotherapy
creator: Jun Lu, Hua Zhong, Baohui Han
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). notherapies represent two of the most critical challenges in oncology today. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases, and in this setting, the challenge of immune resistance is particularly acute. Although multiple immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have been approved as standard-of-care therapies, a substantial proportion of patients either fail to respond initially or eventually acquire resistance. This underscores an urgent unmet need for novel therapeutic strategies in this prevalent malignancy.

title: Prevalence of anxiety and depression and diagnostic utility of the CAT scale in spirometry-confirmed COPD patients: Findings from the Chinese Population Health and Multimorbidities Study
creator: Sinan Wu, Jian Kang, Xiangyan Zhang, Lan Yang, Fuqiang Wen, Yuanlin Song, Jianping Zhao, Jianying Xu, Wen Li, Pixin Ran, Kewu Huang, Yahong Chen, Yanfei Guo, Guangliang Shan, Ting Yang, Chen Wang, Jieping Lei, Chinese Population Health and Multimorbidities Study (CPHMS) Investigators
description: BackgroundPatients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently present with psychological comorbidities, including anxiety and depression, which may contribute to poorer clinical outcomes. However, the prevalence and impact of these mental health conditions in COPD patients have long been underrecognized.

title: Respiratory immunology: an ancient yet emerging interdisciplinary field
creator: Yuqing Lv, Weining Xiong, Bin Cao
description: also as a highly specialized barrier surface that integrates immune surveillance, inflammatory control, epithelial protection, and tissue repair.1,2 Tissue-resident immune cells, epithelial cells, stromal cells, and soluble mediators together maintain a dynamic equilibrium between host defense and immune tolerance at this environmental interface.

title: Roles of orexinergic and noradrenergic neuronal activity in ketamine-induced analgesia: A study using an orexin/ataxin-3 transgenic rat model
creator: Mitsuru Tonosaki, Tetsuya Kushikata, Yoshikazu Nikaido, Daiki Takekawa, Hirotaka Kinoshita, Jyunichi Saito, Kazuyoshi Hirota
description: BackgroundOrexin, a neuropeptide, physiologically interacts with locus coeruleus noradrenergic (LC-NA) activity. We hypothesized that this interaction affects ketamine-induced acute analgesia.MethodsWe assessed ketamine-induced acute analgesia in transgenic (TG) and wild-type (WT) rats with genetically degraded orexinergic neurons using hotplate and tail-flick tests.

title: Obturator hernia misdiagnosed as inguinal incarceration: a case of postoperative small-bowel perforation and subcutaneous fecal emphysema
creator: Anas Derkaoui, Tarik Deflaoui, Intissar Aissi, Abdelali Guellil, Rachid Jabi, Mohammed Bouziane
description: Introduction and importance:An obturator hernia is a rare condition accounting for less than 1% of abdominal wall hernias. Due to its deep pelvic location and nonspecific clinical presentation, it is frequently misdiagnosed, most often as an inguinal hernia. Delayed or incorrect diagnosis may result in bowel ischemia and perforation.

title: Can artificial intelligence-derived bone mineral density outperform traditional morphometric measurements in opportunistic osteoporosis screening using pelvic radiographs? A multicenter comparative diagnostic study
creator: Chia-Che Lee, Xi-Qian Heng, Hung-Kuan Yen, I-Hsin Chen, Tzu-Hao Tseng, Hong-Da Lu, Hung-Chun Lee, Ruey-Feng Chang, Chen-Yu Wang, Shau-Huai Fu
description: ObjectivesTo investigate whether an artificial intelligence (AI) model could demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy in identifying dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) confirmed osteoporosis, outperform traditional human-read metrics, and deliver substantial clinical net benefit.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter cohort study included 382 patients with hip fractures who had both preoperative pelvic radiographs and postoperative DXA scans.

title: Suppression of Elastic Scattering of CH4 by Graphene Passivation of Ni(111)
creator: Amjad Al Taleb, Francesc Viñes, Daniel Farías
description: We report high-resolution angular diffraction measurements of CH4 and Ne from Ni(111) and from a graphene (Gr) layer grown on Ni(111), whose effective atomic mass is enhanced by the strong Gr–Ni interaction. The incident energies are between 43 and 68 meV for Ne, and between 62 and 108 meV for CH4 beams.

title: Fall risk in rheumatoid arthritis revisited: A follow-up study focusing on sarcopenia and glucocorticoid use
creator: Naoki Nakagawa, Keita Nagira, Masako Hayashibara, Takashi Wada, Yuki Kitsuda, Yuta Takasu, Chikako Takeda, Mari Osaki, Hiroshi Hagino, Hideki Nagashima
description: ObjectivesTo re-evaluate fall incidence and its determinants in a contemporary cohort of ambulatory women with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in a follow-up study based on our previously published cohort data.MethodsWe prospectively evaluated 124 ambulatory female patients aged ≥50 years with RA at a single institution in 2022–2023, monitoring falls for 1 year.

title: Change in the life expectancy gap among people with mental illness: a 14-year population-based cohort study in Australia
creator: Mike Trott, David Lawrence, Sean Halstead, Claudia Bull, Dan Siskind, Steve Kisely
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundPeople with psychiatric disorders die substantially earlier than the general population, with life expectancy gaps of 10–20 years reported internationally. Prior Australian data indicated this gap was widening, whereas evidence from other countries has been mixed.

title: Descriptor: Synthetic Genomic Dataset With Diverse Ancestry (SynGen6)
creator: XINYUE WANG, SITAO MIN, JAIDEEP VAIDYA
description: Advancements in genomic analysis techniques and data-driven research are driving precision medicine. However, in many cases, these advances are not equitable and do not help all subpopulations, since many existing genomic datasets lack diversity, limiting their applicability for studying populations beyond those of European ancestry.

title: iProDNet: integrated probabilistic differential network inference under heterogeneous biological conditions
creator: Heewon Park, Seiya Imoto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Understanding phenotype-specific network rewiring is essential for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. Although numerous differential network analysis methods have been developed, most focus on only a limited aspect of network information. Consequently, these approaches often fail to jointly characterize regulatory activity and network architecture, provide limited statistical evidence at the network level, and offer little capability for prioritizing key genes that drive phenotype-specific network rewiring.

title: MHCXGraph: a graph-based approach to detecting T-cell receptor cross-reactivity
creator: Carlos D M S Simões, Rocío L B R Maidana, Samuel C de Assis, João V S Guerra, Helder V Ribeiro-Filho
description: The T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition of multiple peptides presented by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) is a key natural phenomenon, enabling the T-cell repertoire to respond to a broad array of antigens. Despite its importance to the immune response, T-cell cross-reactivity poses a major challenge for the development of novel T cell–based therapies.

title: PEARL: novel protein targets recommendation model via heterogeneous graph representation learning
creator: Zixuan Liu, Jiasi Luan, Zhen Zhang, Kui Tang, Xingyu Qin, Zhixiao Qi, Borui Zhang, Jun Liao
description: Peptide drug repurposing depends on identifying likely protein targets for a query peptide across a large candidate space, yet most existing peptide–protein interaction models are optimized for isolated pairwise classification rather than target prioritization. Here, we present PEARL, a recommendation-oriented heterogeneous graph learning framework for peptide target recommendation.

title: The Pathologic Roles and Therapeutic Implications of Ghrelin/GHSR System in Mental Disorders
creator: Qianshuo Mao, Jinjia Wang, Zihan Yang, Ruidong Ding, Shuangyu Lv, Xinying Ji
description: Ghrelin is a hormone consisting of 28 amino acids. Growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) is a receptor for ghrelin, which is expressed in the brain, pituitary gland, and adrenal glands, especially in the hypothalamus. The binding of ghrelin to the receptor 1a subtype mediates most of the biological effects of ghrelin.

title: Unsupervised identification of low-frequency antigen-specific TCRs using distance-based anomaly scoring
creator: Kyohei Kinoshita, Tetsuya J Kobayashi
description: Identifying antigen-specific T cell receptors (TCRs) within the diverse human repertoire remains challenging, particularly for low-frequency clonotypes.
